column1: # CLAIM_MAP — Wills' (1981) conjecture: the claims of the paper's TeX source v1.90 (md5 0c30e1ff; its table file tab_witness.tex md5 1f8d76d0).
# Columns (TAB, exactly 5 on every data line; "-" = an empty field, since editors strip trailing TABs):
#   claim id | description (lines of v1.90) | REQUIRED rows | SUPPORT rows | KIND.
# KIND "-" = proved rows: status = worst REQUIRED row, hypotheses united (PROVED > PROVED GIVEN <facts/checks> > not
#   proved yet); every row carries, as explicit binders, every fact and check its proof uses.
#   FACT <Prop> = a fact the paper USES from an area Mathlib lacks: an explicit hypothesis in
#   Wills/Facts/Basic.lean, status "not formalized: no <area> in Lean's library".
#   CHECK <Prop>,<Prop> = a computer check: an explicit hypothesis in Wills/Checks/Computations.lean,
#   status "checked by computer, NOT proved in Lean" (log: ./reproduce.sh computation-N).
#   NOT-FORMALIZED faces = a claim about faces of polytopes: "not formalized: no faces of polytopes in Lean's library";
#   facets enter Lean only as the numbers of E3 (IsFacetData) and TRI.
# Quantifier rule: each printed quantifier and exception is compared with the row's type; a row true WITH an exception
#   does not cover a sentence WITHOUT it.
#   g_i = coefficient i of the interpolating polynomial of degree <= n through k = 0..n (EHR: it agrees with L at every
#   k >= 0); every sigma (or NVol) sentence is typed over E3's facet data, sigma = Σ relvol_j, NVol_j = 6 relvol_j, with
#   the fact FacetFormula as a binder (the real facets' data satisfy E3's equations, so the row implies the printed
# NOT COUNTED (no mathematical claim of this paper): history and attributions — abstract l.47 "In 1981 Wills
#   conjectured", "Wills proved this for n <= 3, and Henze showed in 2014 that it fails for every n >= 7; the dimensions
#   4, 5 and 6 remained open"; l.52 "Ehrhart [Ehr62] proved"; l.56 "may be negative [BR15]" (quoted, used by no proof);
#   l.58 "Wills looked for a discrete analog", "Wills called these numbers the expected values", "known as Wills'
#   conjecture; we use Henze's formulation"; l.67 "Wills proved the case i = n-1 in every dimension" (the attribution;
#   the mathematics is claim I9c), "Wills also proved it for n = 3" (used: fact WIL3), the dimension-4 bounds of
#   [Wil81 Thm (iii)], Betke-Henk-Wills, Henze's P_7 and 1534/105 > 14, Henze's root theorem, Henze's Remark 2.2 quote;
#   Table 1 "before" column l.76-79; Figure 1 "Known before" row and caption l.140 first sentence; l.87 "Wills had
#   proved g_1 < 21 and g_2 < 31"; l.89 "Henze's tests ... found no counterexample"; l.90 "and for n >= 7 by Henze's
#   theorem as well" (Theorem 1.3 covers every n >= 5); l.151 "This is the method of [ABS21] and [AS24], who used it
#   for other extremal problems"; l.225 (how W was found, the 58-vertex example); l.248 "this is Wills' argument for
#   g_{n-1}"; l.163 "(Ehrhart, Macdonald)"; l.182 "cf. [Hen14, Prop 2.3]"; l.323 "(Minkowski [Min97]; see Venkov
#   Route, organization and pointers: abstract l.47 ("combines Ehrhart reciprocity, the lower bound theorem
#   ... about three million sets": the sum of the printed counts 2,547,694 + 616 + 588,592 = 3,136,902); l.143 "is a
#   computation", "that any program for counting lattice points can confirm"; l.151 "we enumerated all of them with two
#   independent programs (Section 6)"; l.153; l.192; l.229 notation; l.266 "this is why the computations ... are
#   needed"; l.271 "it remains to prove (star) for G >= 31" (covered by G_odd + lem_4_3); l.275 "Figure 2 shows";
#   l.332 the walk-down description (its claim is W6b); l.367 and l.369 descriptions of the two programs except the
#   claims C5b, C5c; l.387 "We first check". Descriptions of the computer runs (logs in the repository): l.220 "These
#   numbers were computed by four independent programs, among them Normaliz 3.10.2 and LattE integrale 1.7.6; the data
#   and the commands are in [Repo]"; l.330 "exhaustive, exact integer and rational arithmetic, two independently written
#   programs; the two programs agree on every count and every maximum", and how each program computes the Ehrhart
#   polynomial; l.353 "listed once as BZ^4 with B in Hermite normal form"; l.361 "it suffices to take V in Hermite
#   normal form". Remark 4.4 first sentence l.266: a remark on another argument, given in [Goel26]; the dimension-3
#   theorem enters Cor 1.4 as the fact WIL3. Definitions (no claim): l.52-55 L_P; l.58 W^n and C_n; Conjecture 1.1
#   l.60-65 (WillsConj); l.158 isomorphic pairs, unimodular equivalence; l.170 W^n_Λ, G(P); l.251 NVol; l.272-273 M(P),
#   r(P); l.291 saturated; l.307 frame; l.326 frame lattices, A(Λ); l.378-381 T, X.
#   Remarks about this Lean folder (no mathematical claim): the abstract's last sentence l.47 "Theorems 1.2, 1.3 and 7.1
#   and Corollary 1.4 are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the computer computations and some published
#   results as hypotheses" (AUDIT.md lists each row's hypotheses); the footnote l.38 "Lean 4 proof:" with its link.
# ROUTE DIFFERENCES: Cor 1.4 prints "for n <= 3 this is Wills' theorem" and "g_3 <= 32 by [Wil81, Theorem (i)]"; Lean
#   proves n = 1, 2 by conj_le_two (PROVED GIVEN E1, E3), uses the fact WIL3 for n = 3 only, and for n = 4 uses Prop
#   4.2's g_3 <= 2 g_4 <= 32 (PROVED GIVEN E1, E3). Section 7's polynomials: Lean uses L(0), L(1), L(2), L(-1), L(-2)
#   (counting + E2) instead of the facet distances (not formalized).

(E2) l.162: reciprocity L_{P,Λ}(-k) = (-1)^n #(int(kP) ∩ Λ) for k >= 1

l.275: M(P) is finite (P contains a ball around 0) and symmetric; <u,x> in {-1,0,1} for u in M(P), x in P ∩ Z^4
